title: Solstice AI POC scoping - timeline & milestones
next_steps: Jamie to send draft SOW + pricing by 2026-12-15
Ravi to share benchmark plan and required dataset checklist by 2026-12-14
Sofia to provide VPC network contact and sample infra details by 2026-12-14
action_items: Jamie Carter - Draft SOW + pricing - due 2026-12-15
Ravi Shah - Benchmark plan (latency/cost/quality) and perf script - due 2026-12-14
Sofia Perez - Provide VPC peering info, firewall rules, and sample dataset access - due 2026-12-14
Maya Lin - Confirm success criteria and 3 evaluation prompts/human labels - due 2026-12-16
summary: AE+SE align with Solstice AI on a 6-week POC focused on latency/cost benchmarks and quality regressions. Plan: kickoff and infra access (week of 12/20), run baseline benchmarks (last 2 weeks of Dec), midpoint review mid-Jan, exec readout early Feb. Success criteria: 95th p99 latency < 300ms for 512-token seq on dedicated infra OR cost reduction vs current host by 30% with equal quality. Security: SOC2 & SSO needed; Solstice requests private VPC for data-in-flight. Action items and deadlines captured.
topics: Introductions; current stack (inference/EKS, Databricks for data); POC goals; success criteria; workload sizing; benchmark plan; infra/access; timeline & milestones; security/compliance; next steps; exec readout planning
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie: All right folks, thanks for joining. we're at 3pm PT, Jamie Carter from Redwood, ravi's on the call too. quick intro round?
[00:12] Maya: hi all, maya lin, head of ML at Solstice. thanks.
[00:16] Ethan: Ethan Rivers, CTO. we own infra and procurement.
[00:20] Sofia: Sofia Perez, DevOps. i'll handle network and access.
[00:23] Leo: Leo Tan, PM for this initiative.
[00:26] Ravi: hey everyone, ravi shah, solutions engineer - i'll run the benchmark work with you.
[00:30] Jamie: Great. Goal for today is to scope a POC - timeline, milestones, success metrics, what access we need. This looks like a six week timeline but we want to confirm.
[00:40] Jamie: Ethan can you give a quick overview of current stack - where you run models now and traffic shape?
[00:46] Ethan: Sure. right now we run most inference in-house on EKS with g4/v100 nodes for some legacy models and we also use a managed hosted LLM provider for production features - not saying names - but we see inconsistent p99 latency and cost is high. Traffic is spiky, batch jobs overnight for analytics, but real-time product calls peak midday. Our target is faster responses and to bring costs down.
[01:10] Maya: For the prototype stage we mainly want retrieval augmented generation for our support assistant. 512 token responses typical, some longer ones to 1k but rare. We have about 150QPS peak for the assistant, but for the POC we'll simulate 10-30 QPS.
[01:28] Ravi: Good, that helps. Typical sequence is 512 tokens, we should size for 10-30 qps sustained and bursts up to 60. For benchmarks we usually run step load tests and a steady-state throughput run.
[01:40] Jamie: Let's talk success criteria. what would make this a yes for Solstice?
[01:45] Maya: Three things - latency within product SLA (p95 < 200ms and p99 < 400ms for 512 token), parity of quality against our current hosted provider (we'll do blind evals), and a unit cost reduction of at least 25-30%. Security must be enterprise grade - SOC2, SSO, audit logs.
[02:05] Ethan: Also predictable throughput and the ability to run in a private VPC - we can't send token payloads to public endpoints for PHI-ish logs.
[02:12] Jamie: Understood. Redwood supports private deployments and dedicated pools; we can run in a VPC or dedicated. there's some trade offs on latency vs cost.
[02:22] Ravi: Let me outline the POC milestones we recommend: kickoff & access setup (week 1), baseline benchmark (weeks 2-3), optimization + mid-point review (week 4), extended stress tests and RBAC/audit verification (week 5), exec readout and decision (week 6).
[02:40] Leo: That sounds reasonable. can you be more specific on what we need for access?
[02:45] Sofia: yes - we need to know exactly what network setup, sample data endpoints, and credentials to provide.
[02:50] Ravi: For a private deployment we need: VPC peering info or Transit GW details, a service account with limited S3 read to the dataset, and a bastion for logs. For hosted dedicated, we need IP allowlist and sample traffic.
[03:06] Jamie: I'll send a checklist. Sofia, you'll be our contact for infra.
[03:10] Sofia: noted. we'll also need the expected data volumes.
[03:13] Maya: For the POC we'll provide a 50k-turn token synthetic set plus 200 labeled eval prompts for quality checks.
[03:20] Ravi: Perfect. for benchmarks: baseline run (no caching, default batching), then optimized run (batching, KV prefix cache) and then dedicated quantized model run to measure cost + quality. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens.
[03:40] Jamie: On reporting, we'll share a spreadsheet with latency histograms, tail latency, cost calc, and a qualitative evaluation deck.
[03:48] Ethan: What about tooling to reproduce tests? we want to run locally too.
[03:51] Ravi: We'll share load scripts (k6-based) and perf harness; you'll be able to run them against your environment.
[03:58] Maya: timeline questions - there are holidays end of Dec, will that affect kickoff?
[04:02] Jamie: Good call. We planned kickoff week of Dec 20 to get infra config done before holidays. most heavy benchmarking will happen late Dec into early Jan; mid-point review mid-Jan. If holiday availability is low we can shift some runs to first week of Jan but prefer keep momentum.
[04:18] Leo: Who owns the exec readout?
[04:20] Jamie: Redwood will prepare the readout deck; we'll ask Solstice to provide 2 execs to attend and confirm business metrics.
[04:27] Ethan: fine. about cost targets - our CFO wants expected monthly run cost for production at 150 QPS. are you able to extrapolate from POC numbers?
[04:36] Ravi: We'll give a conservative extrapolation based on tokens/sec and GPU types. For a POC we capture unit economics; production estimate will be a modeled extrapolation.
[04:44] Jamie: let's capture the exact success thresholds in the doc: p95 < 200ms, p99 < 400ms for 512 tokens OR if running in dedicated mode p99 < 300ms; cost reduction >=25% vs current hosted baseline; quality delta < 2% on the blind eval (or defined pass rate).
[05:02] Maya: that works. also audit logs retention 1 year and SSO/SAML + roles.
[05:09] Ravi: We support SAML SSO and can ship audit logs to your SIEM; retention configurable. We'll add that to security checklist.
[05:17] Jamie: Any hard constraints we should know - e.g., dataset can't leave country?
[05:21] Ethan: For now data residency in US only is preferred; we can discuss more if needed.
[05:26] Sofia: On the infra side, we'll need a runbook for opening ports and a sample CF/Terraform snippet for peering.
[05:33] Ravi: we'll include Terraform snippets in the access doc.
[05:36] Leo: benchmarks - you mentioned 3 runs. what's the acceptance criteria per run?
[05:40] Ravi: baseline: collect raw numbers; optimized: p99 should be improved 20-40% depending on batching; quantized: cost per 1k tokens reduced but we'll measure quality drift - acceptable drift <= 2% on eval.
[05:51] Maya: for quality tests we'll provide human labels and we want blind A/B.
[05:55] Ravi: that's our plan. we'll host the A/B harness and produce confusion matrices.
[05:59] Jamie: ok wrap up - to confirm milestones and dates: kickoff/access setup week of 2026-12-20, baseline runs 12/28-12/31 (light due to holidays) and heavier runs 01/04-01/10, mid-point review week of 01/18, final stress tests 01/22-01/28, exec readout week of 02/08.
[06:19] Maya: timeline looks good - can you move mid-point if we have resource constraints?
[06:22] Jamie: yes flexible a week earlier or later if needed but we'll try to hold.
[06:26] Ethan: procurement question - do you have a standard POC agreement or do we need legal to review SOW?
[06:31] Jamie: we'll send a draft SOW and standard POC MSA; legal review may take 1-2 weeks. we'll flag critical security clauses to speed review.
[06:40] Sofia: we'll share a contact in networking; expect some firewall approvals.
[06:44] Ravi: I'll also ask our infra team to prepare an attachable demo VM for debugging.
[06:48] Leo: great. any other open questions?
[06:51] Maya: one more - can we request a sanity benchmark on a smaller sample before Xmas?
[06:56] Ravi: yes we can do a smoke test using a 5k token set as soon as we have minimal access - aim to run that by 2026-12-22.
[07:04] Jamie: Perfect. I'll circulate notes and the access checklist. Thanks everyone.
[07:08] Ethan: thanks.
[07:09] Sofia: thanks all.
[07:10] Maya: thanks.
[07:12] Jamie: we'll follow up in the CRM and push the SOW. bye.
[07:15] // End of recording
